candidate_relations.reason: Palms and soles have eccrine, not apocrine, glands; apocrine chromhidrosis is the wrong glandular subtype.
Palmoplantar psoriasis does not explain green-black dermatoglyphic pigment or an eccrine duct filled with amorphous material.
Autoimmune hepatitis is not supported and is not the pigmented sweat diagnosis.
Chromhidrosis is the parent process but omits the eccrine subtype required by the reference.
Pityriasis rubra pilaris does not match eccrine chromhidrosis or the PR-like trunk plaques.
Primary sclerosing cholangitis is not established; the liver disease is alcoholic cirrhosis with extreme hyperbilirubinemia.
Deep-seated palmoplantar vesicles resemble dyshidrotic eczema but the pigment and eccrine-duct contents define chromhidrosis.
Lichen planus is a different inflammatory dermatosis.
Drug-induced liver injury is not the diagnosis for pigmented eccrine sweat.
Psoriasis is not supported by the palmar histology of spongiosis and eccrine-duct material.
Inflammatory dermatosis is a vague parent of the rash, not eccrine chromhidrosis.
Eccrine chromhidrosis matches the reference given palmoplantar green-black pigment and amorphous material in a dilated eccrine duct.
Alcoholic cirrhosis explains extreme hyperbilirubinemia that can color eccrine sweat but is the comorbidity, not the dermatologic diagnosis.
Primary biliary cholangitis is not documented.
A viral exanthem does not explain eccrine chromhidrosis.
Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is the metabolic source of pigment, not the sweat-gland diagnosis.
Chest and thigh biopsies were consistent with pityriasis rosea, a concurrent eruption, not eccrine chromhidrosis.
Alcoholic liver disease is the underlying hepatopathy, not the chromhidrosis.
Cholestasis-induced dermatitis is related pruritus/skin change, not eccrine chromhidrosis.
Cholestatic pruritus is a symptom of liver failure, not the pigmented sweat diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: Palm biopsy showed a dilated eccrine duct with amorphous material plus concurrent pityriasis rosea on trunk biopsies.
